N49_identifiability.signed_age: EXACT_COLLINEAR_WITH_CHOOSER_AND_TARGET_FE, residual norm ratio about 3.48e-11; coefficient intentionally excluded
N49_identifiability.popularity_proxy: Target-level predictor fully absorbed by target fixed effect; cannot estimate distinct popularity coefficient simultaneously
N49_identifiability.target_age_linear: also collinear with fixed target age.

N51_actor_candidate_degree_null.method: Bipartite checkerboard Markov swaps preserve chooser & candidate yes-degree and observed edges per wave, 250 recorded states after 6000 burn attempts and 400 proposals between samples, per gender
N51_actor_candidate_degree_null.validation: Degree sums of every actor and candidate within wave preserved exactly after swaps
N51_actor_candidate_degree_null.limitation: single chain, unknown uniformity/mixing; descriptive reference ranges only, not p-values, resampling assumes fixed graph and no exposure-level endogeneity

N52_target_FE_explained.caveat: in-sample high-dimensional candidate parameters, expected increase in fit, not out-of-sample prediction

N53_mixmosa.adversarial: Previously observed male sign reversal under a different permutation statistic is not a stable general two-way FE effect: Mixmosa men's 2FE age gap is ~0.

N54_prospective_gate.decision: BLOCKED, no prospective out-of-event popularity prediction; do not use same-event votes as holdout

limitations: Speed dating in 2002–04 USA and later Mixmosa foreign data, not Tinder or Spain
Observed candidate acceptability not random independent, common popularity can be latent attractiveness
FE absorbs person-specific constants, cannot separately estimate time-invariant target-level popularity
No prospective independent test; previous data used for iterative model choice
MCMC null unproven mixing; no exact conditional p-values
Two-sided participant correlation not addressed by one-way cluster SE
privacy: no raw rows or pseudonymous participant identifiers posted to GitHub
